text: dsh-starred-turns 是一个适用于 DSH 网页端的轮次收藏插件。它在对话右侧轮次栏中响应右键操作，将对应轮次按会话保存，并通过加长和强调标记帮助用户在长对话中找到重要内容。收藏状态会随轮次栏更新重新绘制，右键同一标记可取消收藏。插件通过客户端 store 持久化，不需要额外 API 密钥或外部服务。

dsh-starred-turns lets DSH web users bookmark turns in the conversation rail. Right-click a marker to save or remove a bookmark for that conversation. Saved markers appear longer and in the accent color, and are reapplied when the rail updates. No API key or external service is required.
我想把长对话里重要的轮次标出来，之后能快速找到。
能不能在对话右侧的轮次导航上收藏某一轮？
I want to bookmark important turns in a long chat and spot them in the turn rail.
dsh-starred-turns 的功能「收藏对话轮次」：在网页端对话轮次标记上右键即可切换收藏状态；被收藏的标记会以强调色和完整长度显示，状态按会话保存并在轮次栏更新后重新绘制。

dsh-starred-turns README · dsh-starred-turns：Bookmark turns from the conversation's right-edge **turn rail** — the column of short dashes where each dash marks one turn and jumps back to it when clicked. A bookmarked dash grows to the rail's full length and takes the accent colour, so a specific turn stays easy to find in a long conversation.

Right-click a dash to bookmark it; right-click again to unbookmark.

[中文说明](README.zh.md)

dsh-starred-turns README · Why：A long conversation gives you a rail of identical dashes. The shipped rail already distinguishes the *active* turn, but nothing lets you mark the turns *you* care about — the decision, the diff, the answer you keep scrolling back to. This plugin adds exactly that one bit per turn, and makes it visible at a glance by reusing the rail's own "full length" geometry.

dsh-starred-turns README · Features：- **Right-click to bookmark a turn.** The dash grows from its resting length (`scaleX` 0.4 for turns not loaded into the transcript, 0.6 for loaded ones) to the rail's full width (`scaleX` 1), and switches from the neutral border colour to the accent colour.
- **Bookmarks are per conversation.** Turn 5 in one conversation and turn 5 in another are different places; the conversation key is the selected Session id.
- **Bookmarks persist.** They survive reloads and, on the Desktop build, app restarts.
- **No layout shifts.** The rail keeps its fixed 10px pitch; only the dash's own `scaleX` changes.

dsh-starred-turns README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin add dsh-starred-turns
```

Or add it to a profile's `cordis.patch.yml` by hand:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: starred-turns
      name: dsh-starred-turns
```

Restart the app (or let HMR rescan) after installing: the Host only scans plugin packages at startup.

dsh-starred-turns README · How it fits in without touching the chat package：The rail is drawn by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-chat` and is not slot-extended, so the plugin decorates it from the outside rather than forking the package. Each dash is:

```html
<button data-index="18" class="…_mark …_markActive" aria-label="Jump to turn 19"></button>
```

with the visible dash supplied by a `::before` pseudo-element:

text: dsh-starred-turns README · How it fits in without touching the chat package：The observer never watches the plugin's own attribute — it writes that attribute, so an unguarded observer would retrigger itself forever. Paints are also guarded by a read of the current attribute for the same reason.

dsh-starred-turns README · Storage：Bookmarks live in a client store named `dsh.starred-turns.v1`, keyed by conversation:

```json
{ "byConversation": { "session-…": ["1", "7"] } }
```

The shell backs `persist` with `localStorage`. On the Desktop build the page origin is the stable `dsh-app://app` scheme, so bookmarks survive app restarts there. On a plain browser the Host picks a new loopback port per launch and browsers scope `localStorage` by origin including the port, so bookmarks do not carry across restarts in that mode.

dsh-starred-turns README · Develop：```sh
npm install
npm run build   # src -> lib (client bundle in the shell's closure-factory format)
npm test        # bundle shape, exported surface, selector targets
```

- `src/client.js` — store, rail painting, right-click gesture, stylesheet
- `src/index.js` — node half (host-side no-op; exists so the Loader has an entry module)
- `scripts/build.mjs` — copies the node half and bundles the browser half with esbuild
